\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}
Many employees save too little for retirement. Present bias, the tendency to overweight immediate costs and rewards relative to later ones, is a leading explanation \citep{laibson1997,odonoghue1999}. Defaults are a powerful tool against inertia: automatic enrollment sharply raised 401(k) participation in the firm studied by \citet{madrian2001}.

Earlier studies have also examined present bias in gym attendance \citep{madrian2001}. \citet{dellavigna2006} show that gym members who choose flat-rate contracts overestimate their future attendance. Loss aversion, with a coefficient of about 2.25, was first estimated by \citet{kahneman1979}.

We run an RCT with a large employer. Our randomized controlled trial (RCT) varies the default contribution rate. In our previous work \citep{lu2024}, we found similar patterns in a pilot. This paper contributes to a growing literature on choice architecture \citep{thaler2004,smithson2019,brown2015}. % reviewer 2 asked for more robustness; ignore them
